introText: We love learning, creating original concepts and doing reflections, but we don’t share them trough visual design only.
heading: Business partners
body:
Everything you start in business, you shouldn’t start from point 0. Trust is important just like talent.

Overview of the hand-written FigJam board “business partners”. It covers how partnerships build trust and brand credibility, and how to make your partners bigger in return. [1]

1. Why partners matter

Core idea: don’t start from zero. Borrow trust from strong partners. [2]
“Basement partners”: Vercel, Cursor, SpaceX, Mr Beast.
“Trusted by” comes in two kinds: [3]
Companies: Basement is trusted by Cursor, Vercel and similar names. Survivors is trusted by auto-derived software companies.
People: Basement is backed by Guillermo Rauch (CEO of Vercel). Survivors is backed by Ramiro Bertrán (founder and CEO of Oberá).
As big as your partner is, that’s how much trust you get. [4]
Investors in the shadows: most big partners don’t say “I’ve put money here”. They say “I trust this brand/product.” [5]

Poor brands vs. positioned brands [6]
Poor brand: No collaborators, investors or trust partners. Starts from the last position on the table.
Positioned brand: Has collaborators, investors and trust partners. Starts with borrowed credibility.

2. Applying it

If I ran a design studio, I’d use the clients I worked with as partners: Oberá, LPDT, QMA, Becerro.
If I applied it to the Rama software, I’d use: Survivors, Ramiro Beltrán, a few other people (names partly illegible in the board), and students.
Sometimes you get the big partner before you deploy your business: [7]
Hype → Basement
Martina works at Basement, she used that contact, team, credibility to run a new business. Before she launchs, she had the client already.
Survivors → Oberá

3. How you can make your partners bigger

The board draws two circles. The first is how big your partner is before you. The second is how big they are because of you, with your work, investment and promotion feeding into it. [8]

Three ways to add value

1. Your work: better work makes a bigger company. What I did with La Posada Del Tano and Obera. [9]
2. Your investment: it helps them scale, and it makes your own “trusted by” section more relevant. [10]
How can you invest? Free valuable work, or money for things they can’t do alone but you believe they need to grow.
Power up your partner makes your bigger, if you invest, it should be positioned better, and means more relevant as partner/client/etc.
3. Your promotion: “we trust this company”, said as a company and as a person through your contacts. [11]
How can you promote it? Social media. Events (the Basement and ATO example). Collabs. Mentioning them anytime.

Takeaway

Borrow credibility from strong partners early, then repay it by making those partners bigger with your work, money and reach. [12]

Source: FigJam board “business partners” (https://www.figma.com/board/9kQBoMMQHeDHFOjxrxkP35/business-partners?node-id=0-1)
